newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Foreign media buys judged on merit-Australia.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Foreign media buys judged on merit-Australia.

text.p: Australian Communications minister Richard Alston said on Wednesday the government would consider foreign ownership of the media on a case-by-case basis.
Alston again ruled out widening the government's cross-media ownership inquiry.

"We don't have any objections to foreign ownership per se, there are obviously situations where a foreigner can bring in a mix of technology, skills, resources, financial or otherwise," Alston told reporters.
"It can make a significant difference, but you make these judgements on a case-by-case basis," he said.

Asked about submisssion to the government's inquiry which claimed that concentration of media ownership would increase if foreign ownership laws were not changed, he said: "We have had a substantial increase in the level of foreign ownership in recent years and I don't know that that has led to any greater diversity in the media."
Media laws currently limit foreign ownership to 25 percent in newspapers and 15 percent in television companies.

Canadian media proprietor Conrad Black has threatened to offload his 25 percent stake in John Fairfax Holdings Ltd, Australia's oldest media group, if Australia does not ease what he called "anachronistic" foreign ownership limits.
Black has said he wanted to lift his stake in Fairfax, which publishes The Sydney Morning Herald, The Age and The Australian Financial Review newspapers, to 50 percent.
